messages.subject: Re: Query on getting Deducer to plot bar graph
messages.subject_clean: Query on getting Deducer to plot bar graph
messages.body_plain:
Without your data, it is difficult to say. You want your data to have two or three columns. one for the x, one for the fill and (optionally) one for the y. Go to Geometric Elements and select bar. In The dialog put the x- variable into the "x" slot. Toggle the fill slot so that you can drop a variable in there and do so. If you want your y-axis to represent something other than the counts of the observations, drop the variable you want to represent in there.

ian

messages.body_plain: I need to plot two or more variables in a single plot, i. e. two or more  variables in a box plot. How can I do it in Deducer? Tanks!
messages.body_snippet: I need to plot two or more variables in a single plot, i. e. two or more  variables in a box plot. How can I do it in Deducer? Tanks!

messages.subject: Re: Two or more variables in plot
messages.subject_clean: Two or more variables in plot
messages.body_plain:
you will need to have your data in "long" format, with one variable representing categories, and the other the values. For example something like:

Variable    Value
cat1          .323
cat1          .33
cat2          .5
cat1          .6

you can then specify "Variable" as the x-axis and "Value" as the y-axis in a boxplot using the plot builder.

ian

I am doing this because I am attempting to create a lab manual using Deducer, as I would for other stats software packages, without the need to teach people how to "code" in R, due to the level of the course.

~John
